# Kit markup reference

This is the class and markup reference of the apple-design web kit that view documents embed. List the blocks a view uses in the `blocks` argument of `show_ui`; the blocks they require are added for you. The kit CSS itself is never read: write markup from these notes. The examples come from ordinary web pages, and nothing in a view loads from the network, so use inline SVG or `data:` URLs for images.

## Blocks

Name, required blocks, purpose:

```text
alert          glass, motion, states        centered modal alert (<dialog>) with 1–3 capsule actions, and a confirmation dialog anchored to its source ([popover]); draws its own actions like UIAlertController
badge          —                            count or dot badge for tab items, toolbar buttons and list rows, with a label that meets 4.5:1 on its fill (COL-3)
base           —                            Document defaults: box sizing, body text and colors, subtree themes, .sr-only, Reduce Motion keyframe stop
button         base, glass, states          Capsule buttons: glass for bars and floating controls, opaque bordered/tinted/filled/plain in content (CMP-3), with pressed, hover, focus, selected, disabled and busy states
card           states                       opaque rounded content card (grouped fill, concentric inner radius), whole-card link via .pressable; never glass (GL-1, CMP-3)
empty-state    —                            empty, no-results or offline placeholder: symbol, title, one-line explanation, optional action
field          states, field-message        text field, text area and search field (clear, Cancel, busy): 44 px box, ≥ 16 px text on touch, focus ring, aria-invalid wired to .field-message
field-message  —                            Inline validation and status text for fields (FB-5)
glass          —                            The one Liquid Glass recipe: members, variants, sheen and glint, token-driven fallbacks
list           base, states                 iOS 26 inset-grouped list: 53 px rows, 20 px inset, 26 px radius, 17 px semibold headers, 13 px footers, pressed/hover/selected/focus rows and switch rows (CMP-7)
menu           glass, motion, states        pull-down menu and generic popover card ([popover]) that pop from their source: 44 px items, leading symbols, checkmarks, separators, destructive and disabled items
motion         —                            Enter/exit (.motion-pop/.motion-fade), stagger, scroll-linked reveal, activity indicator, morph pacing
navbar         toolbar, motion              54 px bar with no background: the large title in the content collapses into the inline title on scroll (scroll-driven, JS fallback)
progress       motion                       determinate progress bar (native <progress> or role=progressbar + --value) and an optional ring; indeterminate = core .activity-indicator
scroll-edge    —                            Soft fade and blur where content scrolls under floating bars, instead of a bar background or divider (GL-7)
segmented      base, states                 32 px capsule segmented control on native radios: sliding thumb that lifts into a glass lens while pressed, 44 px hit rows, auto segment count, RTL
shape          —                            Concentric, capsule and continuous-corner utilities
sheet          base, glass, states          Modal glass sheet on <dialog>: inset at partial height, grabber, centered-title header, scrolling body, detents, spring slide or reduced-motion cross-fade (CMP-5)
slider         states                       native <input type="range">: capsule track, accent fill from --value, white pill thumb that lifts into a glass lens while dragged, optional ticks
states         —                            Generic press, hover, focus, disabled, busy and hit-area states (.pressable, .glass-interactive, .hit-extend)
status-pill    glass                        Glass capsule for off-screen results with an optional Undo (FB-5, FB-9)
stepper        states                       −/+ capsule beside a visible value: hold to repeat (stepper.js), dims at its limits, busy spinner
switch         states                       iOS 26 switch: 63x28 capsule track, 37x24 pill knob at a 2 px inset with 22 px travel, lifting into a glass lens while pressed
tabbar         base, glass, states, button  Floating glass tab bar: 62 px platter, 4 px padding, 54 px capsule items, a sliding selection lens, and a search tab in either current style: a separate round button (button appearance) or an in-row item (standard tab)
toolbar        base, glass, states          Top bar (54 px + safe area) of floating glass capsule groups holding borderless symbol or text buttons (CMP-4)
type           —                            Text-style classes .t-*, font and text-color utilities, CJK tracking reset
type-macos     type                         macOS sizes, weights and tracking under [data-platform="macos"]
```

## alert

```text
== alert  (requires: glass, motion, states)
Alert: only for problems or uncommon, irreversible actions (FB-5, FB-9). Specific title, verb buttons. Cancel keeps
  initial focus for safety (Return can't confirm a destructive action) but is never styled as the default.
    <dialog class="alert motion-pop" id="del" role="alertdialog" aria-labelledby="del-t" aria-describedby="del-m">
      <form method="dialog">
        <h2 class="alert__title" id="del-t">Delete “Trip Notes”?</h2>
        <p class="alert__message" id="del-m">This note will be deleted from all your devices.</p>
        <div class="alert__actions">
          <button class="alert__action" value="cancel" autofocus>Cancel</button>
          <button class="alert__action alert__action--destructive" value="delete">Delete</button>
        </div>
      </form>
    </dialog>
  dialog.showModal() gives the inert background, Esc and focus return; read dialog.returnValue on "close".
  Two actions sit side by side; three (or .alert__actions--stacked for long labels) stack. .alert__action--primary fills the
  one preferred, non-destructive action; never autofocus a destructive one. Slow action: type="button", aria-busy="true"
  aria-disabled="true", an .activity-indicator child and a progressive label ("Deleting…"); close when done (FB-7).
  Confirmation dialog (destructive first; anchored, it has no Cancel: tapping outside cancels):
    <button class="toolbar-btn" popovertarget="trash-ask" style="anchor-name: --trash" aria-label="Delete">…</button>
    <div class="confirm-dialog glass motion-pop" id="trash-ask" popover role="dialog" aria-labelledby="trash-m" style="position-anchor: --trash">
      <p class="confirm-dialog__message" id="trash-m">This photo will be deleted from all your devices.</p>
      <div class="confirm-dialog__actions"><button class="alert__action alert__action--destructive" type="button">Delete Photo</button></div>
      <button class="alert__action confirm-dialog__cancel" type="button" popovertarget="trash-ask" popovertargetaction="hide">Cancel</button>
    </div>
  With CSS anchor positioning it springs from the button (set --motion-origin to the corner nearest it); elsewhere it is a
  bottom action sheet that shows its Cancel row. Reduced motion: .motion-pop fades without scaling; the dim fades (MOT-5).
```

## badge

```text
== badge  (requires: —)
Markup. The number is text, so put its meaning in the host's accessible name:
    <a class="tabbar__item" href="/inbox" aria-current="page"><svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg><span>Inbox</span>
      <span class="badge badge--overlay">3<span class="sr-only"> unread</span></span></a>
    In a list row (inline, trailing): <span class="badge">1</span>
    Dot: <span class="badge badge--dot badge--overlay"></span> plus the meaning in the host's label ("Updates, new").
  .badge--overlay pins it to the top-trailing corner of the host's centred icon (tab items, toolbar buttons).
  Other fills use a COL-3 pair: style="--badge-bg: var(--system-blue); --badge-fg: var(--on-blue)".
  The default red is systemRed darkened so white numerals reach 4.5:1 in light, dark and Increase Contrast
  (systemRed with white is 3.6:1); style="--badge-bg: var(--system-red)" restores the native tone.
```

## base

```text
== base  (requires: —)
Logical properties only (LOC-1: RTL works with dir="rtl").
```

## button

```text
== button  (requires: base, glass, states)
Markup: <button class="btn-filled" type="button">Continue</button>
  Modifiers: .btn-destructive .btn-icon (aria-label required) .btn-block .btn-large.
  Busy (FB-7): aria-busy="true" aria-disabled="true" + <span class="activity-indicator" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  first, and a progressive label ("Saving…"); the indicator itself comes from the motion block: add `motion` to the build.
  Toggles: aria-pressed="true" fills bordered and tinted buttons with the accent (plain: gray fill; glass: tint).
  Labels wrap (balanced) rather than overflow when space runs out, e.g. at 200% text on a narrow phone.
  Size: 44 px by default so the hit region needs no pseudo-element (glass uses both; HIT-1).
  iOS 26 measures a regular .glass button at 34.3 pt and large at 50.3 pt (.btn-large).
```

## card

```text
== card  (requires: states)
Markup. One tap target per card, plus at most one secondary control (components §5.3):
    <a class="card pressable" href="/trips/kyoto">
      <img class="card__media" src="kyoto.jpg" alt="" width="640" height="360">
      <h3 class="card__title">Kyoto</h3>
      <p class="card__subtitle">12 photos · Updated today</p>
    </a>
  With a secondary control, make the card a <div> and the title the link: <a class="card__link" href="…">Kyoto</a>;
  its ::after covers the card and other controls stay on top. .card__media--bleed runs the image edge to edge.
  Separate cards with spacing, not shadows or strokes. On a plain white page set --card-bg: var(--secondary-system-background).
```

## empty-state

```text
== empty-state  (requires: —)
Markup. Say why it's empty and what to do next; never a blank screen or a disabled tab (FB-5):
    <div class="empty-state">
      <svg class="empty-state__symbol" aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 24 24">…</svg>
      <h2 class="empty-state__title">No Results for “kiwi”</h2>
      <p class="empty-state__description">Check the spelling or try a new search.</p>
      <div class="empty-state__actions"><button class="btn-bordered" type="button">Clear Filters</button></div>
    </div>
  Loading instead of empty? Show placeholders or an .activity-indicator with a specific label (FB-7).
```

## field

```text
== field  (requires: states, field-message)
Markup. Give every field a visible label or aria-label, and the right inputmode / autocomplete / enterkeyhint (web.md §11):
    <label class="field__label" for="email">Email</label>
    <input class="field" id="email" type="email" inputmode="email" autocomplete="email" enterkeyhint="next" aria-describedby="email-msg">
    <p class="field-message" id="email-msg">We send the receipt here.</p>
  Invalid (FB-5): aria-invalid="true" on the field + data-tone="error", an icon and the fix in words on the message.
  Checking something slow: <p class="field-message" aria-busy="true"> with an .activity-indicator first ("Checking
  availability…"); aria-busy keeps the indicator turning under Reduce Motion (base block). Remove it when done.
  Search: its own <form>, so type="reset" clears only the query. Listen for `input` AND `reset`. Needs a placeholder.
    <form class="field--search" role="search">
      <input class="field" type="search" name="q" placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" enterkeyhint="search" autocomplete="off">
      <span class="activity-indicator" aria-hidden="true"></span>   (optional: replaces the magnifier while aria-busy="true")
      <button class="field__clear" type="reset" aria-label="Clear text"></button>
      <button class="field__cancel" type="reset">Cancel</button>
    </form>
  In a glass toolbar (CMP-6), put the form inside the glass group and add .field--plain to the input.
  In a list row: <div class="list__row"><label class="list__label" for="nm">Name</label><input class="field field--plain" id="nm">
  (the label keeps its width; the value fills the rest, trailing-aligned).
```

## field-message

```text
== field-message  (requires: —)
Pair each message with its field: aria-describedby, plus aria-invalid="true" on an error.
  The text stays --label: system red is 3.57:1 on white, green and orange ~2.2:1 (fail CON-1 for footnote
  text), so the tone goes on the icon and the field border and the meaning goes in the words.
```

## glass

```text
== glass  (requires: —)
Use: GL-1 functional layer only (bars, controls, sheets, menus) · GL-2 never glass on glass · GL-3 at most
  6 backdrop-filter surfaces per page · GL-4 clear only over media, with .glass-dim for text · GL-5 tint one
  primary action · MOT-6 never animate blur. A new backdrop root (which cuts the blur off from the page) comes
  from filter, opacity < 1, mask, clip-path, backdrop-filter, mix-blend-mode or will-change on an ancestor —
  not from transform (CSS Filter Effects 2, Backdrop Root).
  Members are listed once, here. Custom elements opt in with .glass; components tune the material
  only through tokens on their own selector (--glass-density, --glass-saturate, --glass-blur, --glass-radius).
  Legibility without any fallback (WEB-2: Safari has no prefers-reduced-transparency): with --label
  text the default material passes CON-1 even at the worst backdrop — light 50% white fill (black text 5.3:1
  over pure black), dark 64% #1C1C1E + saturate 130% (white text 4.7:1 over pure white; measured in headless Chrome).
  Members also set a stronger --secondary-label and --destructive-text, so the kit's hints, field labels, list
  headers and destructive labels keep 4.5:1 on glass over busy backdrops; your own glass text stays --label.
  Focus: a focused member keeps its shadows and adds --focus-halo under the ring (FB-6).
```

## list

```text
== list  (requires: base, states)
Markup:
  <h2 class="list-header">Connections</h2>
  <ul class="list list--icons">
    <li><a class="list__row" href="#wifi"><span class="list__icon" aria-hidden="true">svg</span>
          <span class="list__label">Wi-Fi</span><span class="list__value">Home</span><span class="list__chevron" aria-hidden="true"></span></a></li>
    <li><label class="list__row"><span class="list__label">Airplane Mode</span>
          <input class="switch" type="checkbox" role="switch" switch></label></li>   (switch rows don't highlight)
  </ul>
  <p class="list-footer">…</p>
  Selected rows: aria-current="page" or aria-selected="true". Set --list-inset (default 20px) on any ancestor,
  or add .list--flush inside padded containers (sheets set it for you).
  Icon tiles are gray with a white glyph by default; color one with a COL-3 pair, never a hard-coded white glyph:
    <span class="list__icon" style="--list-icon-bg: var(--system-orange); --list-icon-fg: var(--on-orange)" aria-hidden="true">svg</span>
```

## menu

```text
== menu  (requires: glass, motion, states)
Menu (a user-requested list of commands; actions tied to the button that opens it):
    <button class="toolbar-btn" type="button" popovertarget="sort" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Sort">…</button>
    <div class="menu motion-pop" id="sort" popover role="menu" aria-label="Sort">
      <div role="group" aria-labelledby="sort-h">
        <p class="menu__header" id="sort-h">Sort By</p>
        <button class="menu__item" type="button" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="true">Date</button>
        <button class="menu__item" type="button" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false">Name</button>
      </div>
      <hr class="menu__separator">
      <button class="menu__item" type="button" role="menuitem"><svg class="menu__icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg>Share</button>
      <button class="menu__item menu__item--destructive" type="button" role="menuitem"><svg class="menu__icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg>Delete</button>
    </div>
  Symbols for all items of a group or none; destructive last; dim unavailable items (aria-disabled="true"), don't hide them.
  AppleBlocks.menu.init() anchors it to the button (CSS anchor positioning, JS placement elsewhere), sets --motion-origin,
  adds arrow keys / Home / End / type-ahead, toggles aria-checked, closes on choose or Tab (focus returns to the button).
  Without JS it opens centred and keeps Esc / light dismiss; anchor it with style="anchor-name: --sort" on the button and
  style="position-anchor: --sort" on the menu, and close it from items with popovertarget="sort" popovertargetaction="hide".
  Popover (a few related controls, iPad/Mac; a bottom card on narrow screens):
    <div class="popover motion-pop" id="fmt" popover role="dialog" aria-label="Format">…</div>
```

## motion

```text
== motion  (requires: —)
MOT-2: pair each --spring-* with its --dur-spring-*. MOT-4: .motion-pop grows from --motion-origin.
  MOT-5 Reduce Motion: fades stay; scale and stagger go; bounce -> smooth (tokens); essential status keeps
  moving (the base block exempts [role="progressbar"], <progress> and [aria-busy="true"] content from its
  keyframe stop; the rule at the end keeps the spinner's timing in unlayered builds too). MOT-6: transform/opacity only.
```

## navbar

```text
== navbar  (requires: toolbar, motion)
Markup. The bar is the first child of the scroll container, which carries .motion-scroller (motion block; use
  <html class="motion-scroller"> when the page itself scrolls). Button groups reuse the toolbar classes:
    <main class="motion-scroller">
      <header class="navbar">
        <div class="navbar__leading"><div class="toolbar-group"><button class="toolbar-btn" type="button" aria-label="Back">…</button></div></div>
        <span class="navbar__title" aria-hidden="true">Library</span>        (a visual duplicate of the h1)
        <div class="navbar__trailing"><div class="toolbar-group">…</div></div>
      </header>
      <h1 class="navbar__large-title">Library</h1>
      …
    </main>
  Scrolling fades the large title out and the inline title in (opacity + a small rise, MOT-6) over --motion-range, and
  fades in a scroll edge behind the bar (GL-7: no bar background, no divider). --navbar-edge is the page color.
  Without scroll-driven animations, AppleBlocks.navbar.init() toggles .is-scrolled on the scroller; reduced motion swaps.
```

## progress

```text
== progress  (requires: motion)
Markup. Describe the task, not "Loading…" (FB-7); show determinate progress whenever it is known:
    <progress class="progress" max="100" value="40" aria-label="Downloading 12 photos"></progress>
    <div class="progress" role="progressbar" aria-label="Uploading" aria-valuenow="40" style="--value: .4"></div>
    <div class="progress progress--ring" role="progressbar" aria-label="Downloading" aria-valuenow="40" style="--value: .4"></div>
  --value is 0–1. The div form animates its fill on the compositor (MOT-6); the ring needs the div form.
  Indeterminate: <span class="activity-indicator" role="progressbar" aria-label="Loading messages"></span> (motion block),
  never an indeterminate bar, and never swap a spinner for a bar mid-task.
```

## scroll-edge

```text
== scroll-edge  (requires: —)
Markup: first (top) or last (bottom) child of the scrolling element; it takes no layout space.
  <div class="scroll-edge-top" aria-hidden="true"></div> … content … <div class="scroll-edge-bottom" aria-hidden="true"></div>
  Match the page: --scroll-edge-bg (default: grouped background).
  Hidden until scrolling reveals it: the top edge once content has scrolled under the top bar, the bottom edge while
  more content lies below. A scroller with nothing to scroll shows neither, so nothing at rest is blurred.
  No scroll-driven animations (Firefox): toggle .is-scrolled on an ancestor from JS, as navbar.js and motion.md §14.4
  do; it shows both edges.
  Put bar clearance (padding under a floating bar) on an inner wrapper, not on the scroller: the scroller's padding
  moves where sticky edges pin (web.md §5).
```

## segmented

```text
== segmented  (requires: base, states)
Markup (arrow keys move the selection, as in any radio group):
  <div class="segmented" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Filter">
    <label><input type="radio" name="filter" checked><span>All</span></label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="filter"><span>Music</span></label>
  </div>
  2–5 segments (the count is detected); all text or all icons; noun labels. Icon segments name themselves:
    <label><input type="radio" name="view" aria-label="Grid"><span><svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 24 24">…</svg></span></label>
```

## shape

```text
== shape  (requires: —)
GL-6: nested shapes are concentric — inner radius = outer radius - padding.
  <div class="concentric" style="--shape-radius: 28px; --shape-pad: 8px"><div class="concentric-inner">…</div></div>
```

## sheet

```text
== sheet  (requires: base, glass, states)
Markup (open with showModal(): inert background, Esc, ::backdrop scrim; sheet.js adds morph, drag and focus return):
  <dialog class="sheet" id="settings" aria-labelledby="settings-title" data-detent="medium">
    <div class="sheet__grabber" aria-hidden="true"></div>            decorative; drag handle with a 84 x 44 hit area
    <header class="sheet__header">
      <button class="btn-bordered btn-icon" type="button" aria-label="Close" commandfor="settings" command="close">svg</button>
      <h2 class="sheet__title" id="settings-title">Appearance</h2>
      <button class="btn-filled btn-icon" type="button" aria-label="Done">svg</button>
    </header>
    <div class="sheet__body">…</div>
  </dialog>
  Cancel/Close leading, Done trailing (CMP-5); opaque buttons inside the sheet, never glass on glass (GL-2).
  Focus lands on the first control (the grabber isn't focusable). data-detent: medium | large (optional).
  No JS: commandfor/command needs Invoker Commands (newer than the kit's browser floor); sheet.js adds a fallback,
  or call showModal()/close() yourself.
```

## slider

```text
== slider  (requires: states)
Markup (the native input keeps keyboard, VoiceOver and form support):
    <input class="slider" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="40" style="--value: .4" aria-label="Brightness">
  --value is the 0–1 position of the thumb; set it for first paint. AppleBlocks.slider.init() keeps it in sync and sets
  [data-pressed] while dragging (the lens). Firefox fills natively. Ticks: class="slider slider--ticks" style="--slider-ticks: 4"
  draws 5 marks (4 intervals). Pair with min/max symbols or a value field when precision matters (components §4.3).
```

## states

```text
== states  (requires: —)
Generic rules only (web.md §2); each component block styles its own states with the same tokens (FB-3).
  Press tracking: AppleFeedback.initPressStates() sets <html data-press-tracking>, which switches every pressed
  rule from :active to [data-pressed] (touch-down highlight, slop cancel, release in margin; FB-1).
  .pressable draws hover and press as an overlay on the element's own fill: give it a fill with background-color
  (the background shorthand also clears the overlay).
  No JS? iOS Safari applies :active only when a touch listener exists:
    document.addEventListener('touchstart', () => {}, { passive: true });   // = AppleFeedback.enableActiveStates()
```

## status-pill

```text
== status-pill  (requires: glass)
Only for results that land off-screen or an Undo right after an action; never for errors that need a response
  (inline or alert). Keep it until the person acts or moves on. role="status" already speaks it — don't announce().
  <div class="status-pill" role="status"><svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg><span>Added to Reading List</span>
    <button class="btn-plain" type="button">Undo</button></div>
  Motion: add .motion-pop with --motion-origin: bottom and toggle .is-open instead of hidden.
  Centered and as wide as its content (at most 440 px, and 16 px clear of each side), then the text wraps.
  Inside [data-app-frame] it positions in the frame.
```

## stepper

```text
== stepper  (requires: states)
Markup. A stepper shows no value itself, so pair it with the number it changes (the field is the JS-free fallback):
    <label for="guests">Guests</label>
    <input class="stepper__value" id="guests" type="number" min="1" max="12" value="2" inputmode="numeric">
    <div class="stepper" role="group" aria-label="Guests" aria-controls="guests">
      <button class="stepper__btn" type="button" data-step="-1" aria-label="Fewer guests"></button>
      <button class="stepper__btn" type="button" data-step="1" aria-label="More guests"></button>
      <span class="activity-indicator" aria-hidden="true"></span>        (optional, shown while aria-busy="true")
    </div>
  AppleBlocks.stepper.init() adds press-and-hold repeat, aria-disabled at the limits and value announcements.
  data-step is a multiple of the field's step (data-step="10" for big jumps). No JS: the capsule hides, the field stays.
```

## switch

```text
== switch  (requires: states)
Markup: <label class="list__row"><span class="list__label">Wi-Fi</span>
            <input class="switch" type="checkbox" role="switch" switch checked></label>
  Switches belong in list rows, where the row is the label (components.md §4.2). `switch` adds
  Safari's native toggle haptic; role="switch" gives the semantics elsewhere. Theme with --switch-on.
```

## tabbar

```text
== tabbar  (requires: base, glass, states, button)
Markup (tabs navigate, never act or disable: CMP-1, FB-3):
  <nav class="tabbar-dock" aria-label="Primary">
    <ul class="tabbar">
      <li class="tabbar__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></li>                        (must be the first child)
      <li><a class="tabbar__item" href="#today" aria-current="page"><svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg><span>Today</span></a></li>
      …2–5 tabs. In-row search (standard tab, e.g. when another tab is prominent): <li><a class="tabbar__item" data-role="search" href="#search">…</a></li>
    </ul>
    <button class="btn-glass btn-icon tabbar-search" type="button" aria-label="Search">svg</button>   (button appearance: search engages at once; CMP-6)
  </nav>
  Both search styles are current: the separate button is the HIG's button appearance (Search as the prominent tab,
  its default when no other tab is prominent). Selection is aria-current="page". Without the indicator the selected
  item draws its own lens.
```

## toolbar

```text
== toolbar  (requires: base, glass, states)
Markup: <header class="toolbar">
            <div class="toolbar-group"><button class="toolbar-btn" type="button" aria-label="Back">svg</button></div>
            <div class="toolbar-group"><button class="toolbar-btn" aria-label="Share">svg</button><button class="toolbar-btn" aria-label="More">svg</button></div>
          </header>
  At most 3 groups; never mix a text and a symbol button in one group (CMP-4). The single primary
  action is its own <button class="btn-prominent btn-icon"> directly in .toolbar (GL-5, CMP-2).
  Toggle items: aria-pressed (a selected toggle is filled with the accent, so its symbol holds 4.5:1 over any
  backdrop). Separate groups visually with the scroll edge, not a bar background (GL-7).
```

## type

```text
== type  (requires: —)
TYP-1: sizes are rem, so the browser's text size scales them like Dynamic Type.
  Tracking = --tr-* x --tracking-scale (SF Pro table at each style's size). Emphasized weights: .t-emph (TYP-2).
```

## type-macos

```text
== type-macos  (requires: type)
Opt in with <html data-platform="macos"> (or any subtree). macOS has no Dynamic Type; Body is 13/16 (TYP-1).
  Tracking uses the same SF Pro table at the macOS sizes (foundations.md §4); 26pt = +8/1000 em (between the 24 and 28pt entries).
```
